title: The fence: agents build in the backend first (Piece 3, P3-6)
why: Jason, 2026-11-26 (decisions/0179's note "agents work on the backend first"): "get the agents active working on this without them pushing live file, except for the backend, so I can see them work before we point them on the front end"; "Admin does count for backend". A Team page setting, How far Implementation reaches: Backend only (as shipped) or Everywhere; only the Founder changes it (TeamRunner::setReach checks Access::isFounder itself; never a job or an agent), each change in the Team's History with what it was and Change back. It's part of the decision tree's rules (the fingerprint), so a change clears the tree's approval and agents go back to Planning. At Implementation with Backend only, a ticket whose change reaches a page a visitor, member or business sees (by the files it names, against the live mirror's reach map from tools/page-audit/reach.py --fence-map, carried in gauges.json) stops at its brief: its Work queue page says "Front end: waiting for you" with the file, and the report sends its brief to the Founder (brief_to "founder"), never a build session; a backend one goes to a build session as P3-4 does. A ticket naming no file isn't proved backend, so it waits too. Before a build session sends a build for an agent's brief, send.py --team-ticket re-checks it with reach.py on the live mirror and the zip check; one that reaches a public page is refused with the reason, nothing is sent, and the refusal (releases/fence-refusals.json, carried by gauges.py) puts the ticket back at its brief for the Founder. Unchanged: Tier 3, and rule 1 (agents' releases go through the batch until Piece 3 is live). No new outside call, $0. Also: the Work queue's side panel now draws its status lines as the rest of the site does (TvAsk.statuses after it loads). It's built on P3-4 and P3-5 and follows them.
